claim.text: Among seven pinned original SWI and Scryer Prolog programs, SWI 9.0.4 cleanly loads four originals, but merged Rust Gen26 accepts only the known likes.pl program; the three extra SWI-clean core test modules are Rust syntax-rejected and the three Scryer programs produce SWI ERROR diagnostics despite exit zero.
claim.scope: Seven purposively selected unmodified Prolog files from SWI-Prolog/swipl-devel@111385b9 and mthom/scryer-prolog@47f2c4e7; source hash, licensing, ELF64 SWI 9.0.4, Rust 1.85.1 merged Gen26 and Gen24 baseline, independent likes SWI 12-query oracle and historical 264-case Rust comparison.
assumptions: Pinned upstream Git blobs and source files with embedded rights notices are byte-identical to originals
SWI clean_load requires exit0, no stdout and no stderr, not only a successful process status
A true/0 CLI load probe does not establish arbitrary predicate semantics
The three SWI test modules have individual explicit BSD-2 redistribution rights; the wider SWI suite is mixed-license
Scryer root BSD-3 applies to selected examples without an unexamined third-party data dependency
forbidden_promotions: No statistically representative acceptance rate or general ISO/GNU/SWI conformance
No claim that Scryer programmes are semantically invalid because SWI 9.0.4 lacks dialect-specific libraries
No module/CLP feature implementation inferred from the first rejected slash byte
No hardware performance/cycle benchmark or Gen19 ownership optimization

specification.intended_object: A complete seven-item source/licence identity census with raw typed Rust and SWI loader triplets and a nested independent 12-query positive semantic oracle.
invariants: Exactly seven original .pl files and exactly three rights notices from frozen two upstream commits; no source preprocessing
All source Git SHA1 and SHA256 identifiers preserved with source bytes and origin
SWI reference stdout/stderr/exit classified separately, preserving ERROR-bearing zero exits
Frozen Gen24 and Gen26 Rust interpret identical original source with true. and identical max_solutions=1 and max_steps=100000
Original source likes.pl matches twelve fresh independent SWI ordered answers under Gen26 with fixed resource limits
264 previously supported full-output Rust CLI differential cases remain unchanged
known_answer_cases: SWI likes.pl externally authored public-domain positive
SWI core test_list.pl, test_unify.pl, test_bags.pl individual BSD-2 sources
Scryer root BSD-3 licence and original programme source identities
SWI process exit0 with ERROR output is not clean
An accepted Rust source must produce true. newline, exit0 and empty stderr
Negative Rust syntax classification needs exit2 with syntax at byte diagnostic

implementation.representation: Raw exit/stdout/stderr per source and engine with Git blob SHA and SHA256, licence category, optional ERROR/Warning counts, exact per-file classification and full original source files

controls.compute_parity: Same pinned Rust release compiler, architecture, executable profile and input source across both Rust versions; SWI used only as a separate source loader/semantic reference, not for time metrics.
controls.parameter_parity: All source probes use identical original files, Rust max_solutions 1 and max_steps 100000; likes semantic SWI/Rust uses fixed max 32 solutions, max 100000 steps.
controls.sampling_parity: One complete seven-case curated fixed cohort with no random sample, no repeated statistical trial and no post-execution exclusion.
controls.data_access_parity: Same original file bytes, hashes, licence notices and pinned upstream versions provided to Rust/SWI; no source rewrites.

preregistration.prediction: Known likes source remains accepted by Gen26 and produces 12 independent ordered answers. Additional files containing modules, CLP, DCG and libraries may be rejected by Rust or fail SWI loading; no exact new-source success count was predicted.
preregistration.primary_metric: Entire seven-row per-engine loader outcome vector, with SWI clean eligibility subset computed from raw status and source SHA before comparing Rust acceptance, plus fixed semantic/historical guards.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Descriptive exact finite cohort with no inferential distribution; total seven denominator always visible; source origin and reference implementation independence disclosed by programme family.
preregistration.kill_condition: Any original file/licence/blob drift, source adjustment or exclusion, missing SWI version, mislabeled ERROR-bearing exit0, malformed raw tool output, twelve likes semantic mismatch or historical 264-case Rust regression.
preregistration.stop_condition: No new parser features, module rewrites, missing-library substitutions, benchmark sample changes or post-hoc count inflation in this audit.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M for exact seven-case source-loader observations and bounded twelve-case live SWI likes semantics after final-head CI, no broader language-compliance or performance claim.

result.observed: 7/7 original source Git identities and licences validated; 4/7 cleanly load in SWI 9.0.4 (likes and 3 BSD-2 test modules), 3/7 Scryer sources exit0 with ERROR/Warning missing-library diagnostics and cannot serve as clean references. Gen24 Rust accepts 0/7, Gen26 accepts 1/7 (likes); among the four SWI-clean originals Rust accepts 1/4, rejects 3/4 at module-export slash. Original likes matches 12/12 SWI ordered queries; 264/264 historical Rust CLI cases pass.
result.effect_size: Typed seven-row source-loader outcome vector: SWI-clean=4, Rust-accepted among clean=1, SWI-clean Rust-rejected=3, SWI-diagnostic=3. No population effect size or timing metric.
result.uncertainty: Selected seven programmes from two upstream projects rather than complete/rand corpus; original modules may import plunit or libraries, SWI and SWI test sources share authorship, Scryer sources not independently clean in SWI 9.0.4, external semantic oracle applies only to likes.pl.
retired_claims: Any numerical seven-file acceptance fraction is a general Prolog ISO/GNU/SWI conformance rate
SWI process exit zero implies clean source loading, even with ERROR stderr
Scryer source not loadable in SWI 9.0.4 is a semantically invalid Prolog program
Accepting a predicate-indicator slash alone makes module-heavy source runnable
active_remainder: Module declarations and plunit directives remain unsupported in Rust as observed
Additional Scryer dialect libraries absent from chosen SWI reference
A future genuinely independent, SWI-clean original module needs its own module-namespace and query semantics protocol
No native performance or hardware-cycle evidence
